query: A nonprofit is mission-driven but burning out its staff. How should the Guide connect care, structure, purpose, and operational reality?
original_response: Care, structure, purpose, and operational reality are interdependent; burnout occurs when operational reality extracts more than the system can sustainably give, while purpose without structure becomes unfocused, and structure without care becomes coercive. The meaningful tension is between mission-driven purpose and the operational demands that deplete staff—when the organization's structure and incentives treat human energy as an unlimited resource, trust erodes, accountability becomes defensive, and the very mission the nonprofit exists to serve is experienced as depletion rather than fulfillment. This tension is resolvable when structure is designed as trust-centered infrastructure: incentives, accountability, and communication must be calibrated to protect the human capacity required to carry the mission, rather than assuming commitment can absorb any workload.
